hero.kicker: A space game for heroes aged 7 to 12
hero.intro: You are the mission commander! Fly your crew to the Moon, build your base and keep the astronauts safe. Then travel on to Mars.

what.text: Fly a rocket to the Moon
Give the crew air, water and food
Protect the crew from solar storms

hero.real: All numbers, photos and storms come from real NASA data
hero.scroll: Or scroll down to learn about NASA ⬇️

toMoon.landing: Landing at the Moon's south pole...

toMars.leave: Goodbye, Moon! The crew is back on board...
toMars.space: The trip to Mars is long: about 6 months!

MOON_HELLO.title: 🌙 Welcome to the Moon, Commander!
MOON_HELLO.text: Each day: turn on the systems you want, then press "End day". Careful: energy is limited, and every system uses ⚡.

MARS_HELLO.title: 🔴 Welcome to Mars, Commander!
MARS_HELLO.text: A day here is called a "sol". Earth is very far away, so you must rely on yourself. Keep the battery ready for emergencies!

FLR.title: ☀️ Class {class} solar flare!
FLR.text: The Sun gave off a strong flash. Radiation goes up today.

SEP.title: ⚠️ Solar particle storm!
SEP.text: Fast particles are coming from the Sun. This is the most dangerous thing for astronauts.

CME.title: 📡 Early warning: a solar cloud is coming!
CME.text: The Sun threw out a huge cloud at {speed} km per second. It may arrive in 1 to 3 days. Get ready!

CME_ARRIVAL.title: 🌩️ The solar cloud has arrived!
CME_ARRIVAL.text: The cloud we warned you about is here.

DUST_WARN.title: 📡 Warning: a dust storm is coming!
DUST_WARN.text: In two days a dust storm will cover the Sun for 3 days. The solar panels will make very little energy. Save energy in the battery or buy the reactor!

DUST.title: 🌪️ Dust storm!
DUST.text: Dust is covering the Sun. The solar panels make only a quarter of their energy today.

FAULT.title: 🔧 The greenhouse broke down!
FAULT.text: The greenhouse water pump stopped. Will you ask Earth what to do, or fix it yourself?

event.shelterCost: Dose drops to {dose}, but science and the greenhouse stop today

fact.title: 💡 In real life...
fact.MOON_HELLO: On the Moon's surface, radiation is about 1.369 millisieverts per day. That is 2.6 times more than on the space station!
fact.MARS_HELLO: A sol (a Mars day) lasts 24 hours and 39 minutes. Radiation on the surface of Mars is about 0.64 millisieverts per day.
fact.FLR: NASA records every solar flare in a database called DONKI, and this flare is one of them.
fact.SEP: NASA does not let an astronaut take more than 250 millisieverts from one solar event. That is why spacecraft have a storm shelter.
fact.CME: Mission control watches the Sun every day and warns astronauts before a storm arrives.
fact.CME_ARRIVAL: NASA designs space habitats with a built-in storm shelter where the crew can hide.
fact.DUST_WARN: Dust storms on Mars can last weeks or months! That is why NASA is developing a small reactor that makes 40 kilowatts without sunlight.
fact.DUST: Dust storms on Mars can last weeks or months and cover the whole planet.
fact.FAULT: A message from Mars to Earth takes 3 to 22 minutes, and the answer takes just as long. From the Moon it takes only 1.3 seconds!
fact.NIGHT: Night on the Moon lasts 14.5 Earth days. That is why NASA is developing a small reactor that makes 40 kilowatts without sunlight.

night.title: 🌑 The lunar night is coming!
night.text: In two days a long night begins, and your site gets no sunlight at night. The battery alone is not enough.
night.cant: You don't have enough points for the reactor. Save energy in the battery and turn off what you don't need.

end.life: 🚀 The crew came home safely, but early
end.lifeWhy: Life support ran out. The crew needed more oxygen, water and food than the base could make.
end.radiation: 🚀 The crew came home safely, but early
end.radiationWhy: The crew collected too much radiation, so mission control brought them home to keep them healthy.
end.noStorms: No dangerous storms in this round

final.title: 📋 Commander's report
final.intro: You finished the journey from the Moon to Mars! Here is how you did:

tips.shelterGood: ✅ You sent the crew to the shelter during storms. That is exactly what NASA planners do!
tips.shelterBad: 🛡️ During a solar storm, send the crew to the shelter. You lose a day of science, but you protect their health. NASA's limit is 250 millisieverts per storm.
tips.lifeGood: ✅ You kept the crew's air, water and food going. Great work!
tips.lifeLow: 🫁 Keep life support on every day, and run the greenhouse when you have energy. The crew needs oxygen, water and food every day.
tips.nightPlan: 🌑 Before the lunar night, save energy in the battery or buy the reactor. The night lasts 14.5 days!
tips.dustGood: ✅ You got ready for the dust storm before it arrived. Real commander planning!
tips.dustPlan: 🌪️ When a dust storm warning arrives, pause experiments and save energy in the battery, or buy the reactor.
tips.scienceGood: ✅ You collected lots of science without risking the crew. That is the right balance!
tips.scienceLow: 🔬 On calm days, run experiments and go outside. That earns more stars.
tips.evaStorm: 👩‍🚀 Don't send the crew outside during a storm: radiation outside is doubled.
tips.faultWait: 📡 You waited for Earth's reply. On Mars the answer is slow, so sometimes the crew must fix things alone.
tips.faultFix: ✅ You fixed the problem yourself. Mars crews must rely on themselves because Earth is far away.

nasa.title: NASA: the US space agency
nasa.intro: NASA was founded in 1958. Its job is to explore space, study Earth, the Sun and the planets, and send astronauts and robots to places no one has reached before.

ach.title: First humans on the Moon
ach.text: On the Apollo 11 mission, astronauts walked on the Moon for the first time. Between 1969 and 1972, 12 astronauts walked on it.

ach.title: A home in space
ach.text: Since November 2000, astronauts have lived on the International Space Station every single day, without a break!

ach.title: A robot and a helicopter on Mars
ach.text: The Perseverance rover landed on Mars with Ingenuity: the first aircraft to fly on another planet.

ach.title: An eye on the first stars
ach.text: The James Webb Space Telescope sent its first color images. It sees stars and galaxies that are very, very far away.

ach.title: Back to the Moon
ach.text: On the Artemis II mission, 4 astronauts flew around the Moon and photographed Earth setting behind it.

nasa.supportTitle: How does NASA look after astronauts?

support.title: Underwater training
support.text: Astronauts train in their suits inside a giant pool, because floating in water feels like floating in space.

support.title: Mission control
support.text: A team on Earth watches the mission day and night and warns the crew about solar storms.

support.title: Exercise every day
support.text: On the space station, the crew exercises about two hours a day to keep muscles and bones strong.

support.title: Clean water
support.text: The space station cleans and reuses 98% of its water.

support.title: Storm shelter
support.text: Spacecraft and habitats have a protected place where the crew hides during solar storms.

support.title: Fresh food
support.text: Astronauts have grown lettuce in space and eaten it, using a device called Veggie.

nasa.trainingCaption: An astronaut getting ready for underwater training

astro.title: How do you become an astronaut?
astro.intro: Every astronaut was once a child who looked up at the sky and asked questions. You can start today!
astro.nowTitle: 6 things you can do right now

now.title: Ask lots of questions
now.text: Why is the sky black in space? How does a rocket fly? Scientists always start with a question.

now.title: Love science and math
now.text: They are the language of space. Every rocket flew because someone got the math right.

now.title: Read and learn languages
now.text: Astronauts work with people from all over the world, so they learn other languages.

now.title: Play sports and learn to swim
now.text: Astronauts must be healthy, and they must pass a swimming test.

now.title: Work in a team
now.text: Nobody succeeds alone in space. Help your friends and listen to their ideas.

now.title: Never give up
now.text: In 2021 more than 12,000 people applied to NASA, and it chose only 10. The ones who made it tried many times.

astro.laterTitle: When you grow up: what does NASA ask for?
later: 🎓 A master's degree in science, engineering, math or medicine
🧑‍🔬 3 years of work experience, or 1,000 hours flying as a jet pilot in command
❤️ Passing the medical exam for long space flights
🧑‍🚀 Then about two years of training: swimming, flying, robotics and spacewalks
astro.worldTitle: Space is for the whole world
astro.world: NASA chooses American astronauts, but many countries have space agencies. In 2023 Emirati astronaut Sultan Al Neyadi lived on the space station for 6 months and did a spacewalk, and Rayyanah Barnawi reached the station as the first Saudi woman astronaut.

sources.title: Where do the numbers come from?
sources.intro: Every science number in the game has a source. Numbers marked "simplified" are game numbers we made easier for kids.
sources.donki: The solar storms in the game are real, from the NASA DONKI archive (CCMC). They are stored data, not live, and each event shows its real date.
sources.imgNote: All photos come from NASA's image library. The animations and the logo are our own drawings.
sources.aiText: We used an AI assistant (Claude) to help write the code and text. No AI-generated images are used.
sources.disclaimer: A student project by Team MME for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.
